state:
Project: Telegram-to-web document archive (Papra-style), single admin user, self-hosted.
- A Telegram bot is added as admin to a channel. The channel admin uploads documents (pdf, docx, txt, csv, etc.) to the channel.
- The bot ingests each uploaded document, applies auto-tagging rules (e.g. filename contains `manual` case-insensitively -> tag `Manual`), stores metadata in SQLite, and a Go-served web UI lists documents filterable by tag; clicking a document opens its Telegram message link so the admin can download it from Telegram.
- Backend: Go, single binary, SQLite database (user just confirmed SQLite).
- Frontend: must imitate Papra's look: minimalistic, dark-mode-first, shadcn-style cards, tags as small rounded pills. Papra's real stack is SolidJS + Shadcn Solid + UnoCSS + Hono + Drizzle (its docs site is Astro). Hard constraint: NO TypeScript toolchain; frontend must be Go-served.
- Constraints: runs on a Windows home-server or small VPS; may or may not have a public HTTPS URL; single tenant (one channel, one admin) for v1.
- Verified Telegram Bot API facts: bots CANNOT fetch past channel history via the Bot API (no method exists); they only receive updates for messages posted after being added as channel admin (`channel_post` updates include document attachments). Private-channel links `t.me/c/<chatid>/<msgid>` work only for channel members; `t.me/<username>/<msgid>` works for public channels. Bot API `getFile` download is capped at 20 MB.

update_transport.instructions: How should the Go bot receive Telegram updates, given it may run behind NAT without a public HTTPS URL?

criteria.long_polling: Bot calls getUpdates in a loop; no public URL or TLS needed; works behind NAT; slight delay.
criteria.webhook: Bot exposes an HTTPS endpoint Telegram calls; needs public URL and TLS; instant updates.
criteria.both: Long polling by default with optional webhook mode behind a config flag; more code to maintain.

botlib.instructions: Which Telegram Bot API approach should the Go backend use?

criteria.stdlib: Call the Bot API directly with net/http and hand-written update structs; zero dependencies, full control, more boilerplate.
criteria.go-telegram-bot-api: github.com/go-telegram-bot-api/telegram-bot-api/v5 - classic wrapper, stable but largely unmaintained since 2022.
criteria.go-telegram/bot: github.com/go-telegram/bot - actively maintained, supports long polling and webhooks, modern context-based API.

storage_mode.instructions: What should be stored for each ingested document, given the web UI must open Telegram message links for access?

criteria.metadata_only: Store filename, size, mime, chat/message ids, tags in SQLite; file bytes stay in Telegram only; UI links out to t.me.
criteria.cache_copy: Also download each file once into a local files/ dir; downloads still work if Telegram is unreachable; uses disk.
criteria.lazy_download: Store metadata; download through the bot only when the user clicks download in the UI; note the 20 MB bot getFile cap.

web_arch.instructions: How should the Go web UI be built, given the no-TypeScript constraint and the desire to imitate Papra?

criteria.server_templates: Go html/template renders full pages, plain forms/links for filters; simplest, no JS build step; page reloads on filter.
criteria.htmx: Server-rendered templates plus htmx for tag filter/search without page reloads; one small JS file, no build step.
criteria.spa: Static SPA calling a JSON API from Go; closest to Papra's own architecture but adds a JS/TS toolchain.

frontend_framework.instructions: How should the Papra-like styling be implemented in the Go-served frontend?

criteria.tailwind_cdn: Utility classes matching the shadcn look, loaded via a CDN script tag; no build step; needs internet on first load.
criteria.vanilla_css: Hand-written small CSS file with CSS variables mimicking shadcn tokens; zero external dependencies, fully offline.
criteria.unocss_build: UnoCSS like Papra itself, but needs a Node build step, contradicting the no-TS constraint.

db_lib.instructions: Which SQLite driver/approach for the Go backend on Windows?

criteria.modernc: modernc.org/sqlite - pure-Go driver, no CGO, cross-compiles easily; slightly slower.
criteria.mattn: mattn/go-sqlite3 - battle-tested but needs CGO; on Windows requires a gcc toolchain.
criteria.sqlc_mattn: sqlc codegen over mattn/go-sqlite3; type-safe queries but adds a codegen step and CGO.

rule_engine.instructions: How powerful should the auto-tagging rule engine be in v1?

criteria.filename_contains: Only rule type: filename contains word X (case-insensitive) -> tag Y. Matches the stated example exactly; minimal UI.
criteria.papra_full: Field (filename/extension/mime) x operator (contains, equals, starts with, regex) x value, multiple conditions per rule; mirrors Papra's engine; bigger UI.
criteria.contains_plus_ext: Filename-contains rules plus an extension-based rule type (e.g. ext = csv -> tag Data); middle ground.

tags_per_rule.instructions: When a rule matches a document, how many tags can it assign?

criteria.single: Each rule assigns exactly one tag when it matches; simpler model, matches the example.
criteria.multiple: A matching rule can assign several tags at once; more flexible, slightly more UI.

frontend_style.instructions: On a 0-6 scale, how closely should the web UI copy Papra's visual design?
criteria: Plain functional HTML, no theming at all.
Basic dark background and readable text, nothing more.
Dark theme with simple cards and colored tag pills.
Solid Papra-inspired look: dark-first palette, card grid, pill tags, decent spacing.
Close imitation: shadcn-style tokens, rounded cards, hover states, filter bar styled like Papra's.
Near pixel imitation of Papra's UI including sidebar layout, icons, and empty states.
Pixel-perfect clone attempt of Papra including animations and micro-interactions.

auth_password.instructions: Should the web UI be protected by a single admin password with a session cookie, given document metadata is private but the instance may run on a trusted LAN?

criteria.true: Yes, add a simple password gate and session cookie.
criteria.false: No auth; assume trusted LAN only.

reuse_existing_channel.instructions: Given the verified Telegram facts in the state (bots cannot read history, only new channel_post updates), is reusing an existing channel acceptable for this project?

criteria.true: Reusing an existing channel is fine; old documents are simply absent, new uploads are ingested.
criteria.false: Reusing an existing channel is a real problem; a fresh dedicated channel is required.

multi_org.instructions: Should v1 support multiple channels/organizations with separate document sets, or be strictly single-tenant?

criteria.false: Single tenant in v1: one bot, one channel, one admin, one document list.
